overall.rationale: Unassessable. Korea is the market where these adjacencies are most plausibly developed, which makes the void conspicuous rather than benign — but plausibility is not evidence, and no force can be rated. A further structural problem: 'emerging_adjacencies' is not one market. Any single rating over six sub-segments with different buyers, channels, supply chains and regulators would be meaningless even once data lands, so the research priority is per-sub-segment sizing, not a segment total.

supplier_power.rationale: There is a real, unusual split visible in the repo but not enough to rate it: one Korean-derivative Indian brand manufactures in India (Pilgrim's Korean Rice Water range is made-in-India), while another manufactures in Korea and imports (Limese's formulations are made in Korea, tuned for Indian skin). Those two models have opposite supplier-power profiles — commoditised domestic contract fill versus dependence on an overseas maker plus CDSCO clearance — and with two brands and no cost, margin or volume data, the balance between them is unknown.

new_entrant_threat.rationale: Scoped to ONE of the six sub-segments — kbeauty_derivative. The other five (beauty_devices, ingestible_nutricosmetics, halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal, clean_vegan) have no India evidence and are NOT covered by this rating. Within kbeauty_derivative the entry record is explicit and recent: three Indian D2C brands have already launched Korean-derivative lines — Pilgrim's Korean Rice Water range (made-in-India, vegan), Limese's Korea-manufactured formulations tuned for Indian skin, and Foxtale's Hula Hoop launched amid Korean-inspired demand as it pivots from single-label D2C to a house of brands. The capital for that is documented too: KOSE put US$30m into Foxtale, and India D2C beauty/wellness drew ~US$757m over 18 months. On the make side, brands do not need factories — private-label houses take orders from ~500 units. Named entrants, documented funding and a commoditised make is a live, low-friction entry pipeline. THIN because the evidence is a launch-and-funding record rather than a measured sub-segment: there is no kbeauty_derivative market size, so the rate of entry cannot be set against the size of the prize.

substitutes.rationale: The kbeauty_derivative adjacency is itself best understood as a substitute — an India-made, India-priced alternative to imported K-beauty, which is why the brands market Korean rituals and ingredients rather than Korean origin. But the repo holds no head-to-head price, share or volume evidence between derivative lines and imported K-beauty, so the direction is describable and the pressure is not measurable.

overall.rationale: No segment-level attractiveness call is possible, and arguably none should ever be made for this container: six adjacencies with different buyers, regulators and supply chains do not share an attractiveness read. One signal is real and worth carrying forward — the kbeauty_derivative adjacency has live, funded, named entrants and a commoditised domestic make, which is the corridor's second India-side response alongside the platform land-grab. It is also the adjacency closest to the corridor's ranked whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3), since a made-in-India Korean-ingredient line is precisely how an entrant would hold a genuine Rs700-1500 shelf price rather than a promotion-dependent one. That is a direction, not a rating: with no size for the sub-segment, no price points for the derivative brands and no shares, the segment stays unrated.
